# Lifecycle and GameContext

- [`up.core.GameContext`](#core-GameContext)
- [`up.core.GameProtocol`](#core-GameProtocol)

[Task index](core.md) · [Drawing](drawing.md) · [Testing](testing.md)

Portable gameplay imports only `unpolished-peas`. A game provides
`init(*Game, *GameContext) !void`, `update(*Game, *GameContext, f32) !void`,
`draw(*Game, *GameContext) !void`, and optionally deinit with init's shape.
The host owns the loop. Put simulation and input handling in fixed updates;
draw may run without an update or after several catch-up updates.

The minimal portable game below requests text input, moves once per right-held
tick, copies committed UTF-8 into its own bounded buffer, and draws. It is not
a text editor: composition/preedit is deliberately excluded from committed
state, and the built-in debug font has limited glyph coverage.

[Compiled source](../../examples/api_reference_recipes.zig#L6) (`Game`):

```zig
pub const Game = struct {
    x: i32 = 40,
    name: [64]u8 = .{0} ** 64,
    name_len: usize = 0,

    pub fn init(_: *Game, ctx: *up.core.GameContext) !void {
        try ctx.setTextInput(true);
    }

    pub fn update(self: *Game, ctx: *up.core.GameContext, _: f32) !void {
        if (ctx.input.isDown(.right)) self.x += 1;
        for (ctx.input.extended.eventSlice()) |event| {
            if (event.kind != .text_commit) continue;
            const text = ctx.input.extended.eventText(event);
            if (text.len > self.name.len - self.name_len) continue;
            @memcpy(self.name[self.name_len..][0..text.len], text);
            self.name_len += text.len;
        }
    }

    pub fn draw(self: *Game, ctx: *up.core.GameContext) !void {
        const canvas = try ctx.requireCanvas();
        canvas.clear(up.core.Color.black);
        canvas.fillRect(self.x, 8, 4, 4, up.core.Color.white);
        canvas.drawText(self.name[0..self.name_len], 2, 2, up.core.Color.white);
    }

    pub fn deinit(_: *Game, ctx: *up.core.GameContext) !void {
        try ctx.setTextInput(false);
    }
}
```


A native entry point calls `sdl.playGame(Game)` from the separate
`unpolished-peas-sdl3` import. The [complete compiled tutorial](../../examples/tutorial_game_protocol.zig)
shows that wrapper; generated projects supply their browser wrapper too.

## Ownership, defaults and errors

GameContext borrows host capabilities. Do not deinitialize its Canvas, Audio
or SaveStore, or retain per-tick input/event views. The allocator is supplied
by the host; Image/Font/ActionMap/RenderSurface values created with it belong
to the game and must be released in its deinit callback.

A bare `GameContext.init` contains only input; allocator/canvas/audio/saves/
text input are optional. Normal protocol hosts provide them, but require/check
only the capabilities the game needs. The require methods report
`CanvasUnavailable`, `AllocatorUnavailable`, `Renderer2DUnavailable`,
`SaveDataUnavailable` or `AudioUnavailable`; text requests can return
`TextInputUnavailable`. Audio readiness is separate from its presence.

GameProtocol borrows Game and context; it does not allocate or own the game.
It rejects repeated init, updates/draws before init, invalid elapsed time and
alpha outside [0,1]. Callback errors retain their original cause and phase.
After successful init the host calls optional deinit once, while capabilities
are alive. **If init fails, deinit is not called:** use errdefer to release any
resources loaded before the failure. See the
[collection cleanup recipe](../guides/asset-recipes.md#one-owner-stable-borrowed-resources).

<a id="core-GameProtocol-deinit"></a>
### `up.core.GameProtocol(Game).deinit`

[Source declaration](../../src/app.zig#L146).

Calls an optional game-owned cleanup callback once. Hosts invoke
this before they release context capabilities, so a protocol game
can safely deinitialize resources created through `ctx.allocator`.

```zig
pub fn deinit(self: *Self, context: *GameContext) !void;
```

<a id="core-DeterministicRng"></a>
## `up.core.DeterministicRng`

[Source declaration](../../src/rng.zig#L19).

A small deterministic pseudo-random generator for game simulation.

This is PCG XSH-RR 64/32 with the fixed stream increment from the PCG
reference implementation. `init` uses the documented PCG two-step seed
sequence: advance zero state once, add the supplied `u64` seed, then
advance once more. That recurrence and the output permutation are Peas's
v1 random-sequence contract.

[`algorithm`](#core-DeterministicRng-algorithm) · [`init`](#core-DeterministicRng-init) · [`nextU32`](#core-DeterministicRng-nextU32) · [`nextU64`](#core-DeterministicRng-nextU64) · [`uintBelow`](#core-DeterministicRng-uintBelow) · [`float01`](#core-DeterministicRng-float01)

Fields, variants and defaults (methods follow):

```zig
struct {
    state: u64,
}
```


<a id="core-DeterministicRng-nextU64"></a>
### `up.core.DeterministicRng.nextU64`

[Source declaration](../../src/rng.zig#L47).

Combines two consecutive `nextU32` outputs with the first as the high
half. It is stable as long as the v1 `nextU32` sequence is stable.

```zig
pub fn nextU64(self: *Self) u64;
```

<a id="core-DeterministicRng-uintBelow"></a>
### `up.core.DeterministicRng.uintBelow`

[Source declaration](../../src/rng.zig#L53).

Returns a uniform integer in the half-open interval `[0, upper)`.
Rejection sampling avoids modulo bias. A zero upper bound is invalid.

```zig
pub fn uintBelow(self: *Self, upper: u32) error{InvalidUpperBound}!u32;
```

<a id="core-DeterministicRng-float01"></a>
### `up.core.DeterministicRng.float01`

[Source declaration](../../src/rng.zig#L65).

Returns one of exactly 2^24 equally spaced `f32` values in `[0, 1)`.
It uses the upper 24 bits of one `nextU32` output, so no platform RNG
or floating-point rounding policy contributes to its construction.

```zig
pub fn float01(self: *Self) f32;
```



The RNG owns plain game state. Seed it from `ctx.simulation_seed` during init
when reproduction matters; it does not make wall-clock or arbitrary floating
point game code deterministic. [The testing guide](../guides/testing.md)
explains controlled saves and session identity.
